# Notes for how 16S strains are prepared

## Description

This recipe builds the 16S reference for the 2026 course. It is copied from
`teaching_material/source/analysis_test_data.qmd` (2025), sections "Get genomes
and 16S sequences" and "Investigate 16S amplicon sequence". The commands were adjusted as needed for the new 2026 version.

Where this runs:

- All code runs on Crunchomics in `/home/${USER}/personal/teaching/2026/miceco/prep_16S`.
- All relative paths (`data/`, `results/`, `scripts/`) start in this folder.
- The local folder `16S_prep` (next to `teaching_material`) is a partial copy
  for local checks only.
- This file is a copy of `16S_prep/prep_16S_2026.qmd`, made when the prep was
  finished (2026-11-06). The copy in `16S_prep` is the working version.

Strains for 2026 (ground truth: `teaching_material/data/strains_2026.tsv`):

| ID            | Genus             | Source    | Group | Role 2026      |
|---------------|-------------------|-----------|-------|----------------|
| GCF_000009425 | Lactococcus       | NCBI      | human | community      |
| GCF_000253315 | Streptococcus     | NCBI      | human | community      |
| GCF_000714595 | Escherichia       | NCBI      | human | community      |
| GCF_002055965 | Bacillus          | NCBI      | human | community, new in 2026 |
| GCF_014058685 | Lactobacillus     | NCBI      | human | reference_only |
| LjRoot60      | Pseudoxanthomonas | AT-sphere | root  | community      |
| LjRoot59      | Pseudomonas       | AT-sphere | root  | community      |
| Root401       | Pseudomonas       | AT-sphere | root  | community      |
| Root935       | Flavobacterium    | AT-sphere | root  | community      |
| LjRoot44      | Microbacterium    | AT-sphere | root  | community      |
| Root68        | Pseudomonas       | AT-sphere | root  | reference_only |
| LjRoot303     | Streptomyces      | AT-sphere | root  | reference_only |

Files that go back into `teaching_material/data/`:

- `amplicons_nr.fasta`: this is `data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final.fasta` from this recipe.
- `accession_to_genus.tsv`
- `<id>.fasta.gz`: the 16S sequences of one strain (student files in `cli.qmd`).

## Get genomes and 16S sequences

Strain names were provided by the lab staff. The info was used to download the
assemblies and rRNA sequences from
[AT-sphere](https://www.at-sphere.com/ccquery/ccview/?sort=-GFFs) into
`data/16S` and `data/genomes`. These genomes already have the genomeID in the
fasta header, so no cleaning needed to be done for those genomes.

AT-sphere download links (checked 2026-11-06):

- Genome: `https://www.at-sphere.com/download/assemblies/<ID>.fna.gz`.
  Headers look like `>LjRoot60_contig_1`.
- 16S: `https://www.at-sphere.com/download/rRNA_sequences/<ID>.fasta.gz`.
  On the web page, this column only shows after selecting "rRNA sequences"
  under "Filter Columns". Each file has 1 sequence with the header `>ID`.
  For all 7 root strains the sequence is identical to the 2025 file in
  `teaching_material/data/<ID>.fasta.gz`.
- The `http://` links redirect to `https://`.

The genomes from NCBI were first downloaded and some initial cleaning of the
header done for standardization of the two sources.

```{bash}
mkdir -p data/genomes data/16S 

# Genome
## Download 5 NCBI genomes
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/014/058/685/GCF_014058685.1_ASM1405868v1/GCF_014058685.1_ASM1405868v1_genomic.fna.gz
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/009/425/GCF_000009425.1_ASM942v1/GCF_000009425.1_ASM942v1_genomic.fna.gz
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/253/315/GCF_000253315.1_ASM25331v1/GCF_000253315.1_ASM25331v1_genomic.fna.gz
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/714/595/GCF_000714595.1_ASM71459v1/GCF_000714595.1_ASM71459v1_genomic.fna.gz
# Added 2026: B. subtilis NCIB 3610
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/002/055/965/GCF_002055965.1_ASM205596v1/GCF_002055965.1_ASM205596v1_genomic.fna.gz

ll *gz | wc -l 

## Parse NCBI genomes
gzip -d *gz

for file in *fna; do
  genome=$(echo $file | cut -f1 -d ".")

  echo "Processing $genome..."

    sed -E "/^>/ {
    s/^>/>${genome}-/;   # prefix genome name
    s/ .*//;             # remove anything after first space
    s/\./_/g;            # replace dot with underscore
    }" "$file" > data/genomes/${genome}.fna
done

rm *fna

# Sanity checks 
## All files generated and note empty 
## Header looks as expected: >GCF_000009425-NC_009004_1
ll data/genomes/
head data/genomes/GCF_000009425.fna

## Added 2026: download AT-sphere genomes (root strains) directly into data/genomes
## (not into the working folder, else the NCBI loop above would prefix them)
wget -P data/genomes https://www.at-sphere.com/download/assemblies/LjRoot60.fna.gz
wget -P data/genomes https://www.at-sphere.com/download/assemblies/LjRoot59.fna.gz
wget -P data/genomes https://www.at-sphere.com/download/assemblies/Root401.fna.gz
wget -P data/genomes https://www.at-sphere.com/download/assemblies/Root935.fna.gz
wget -P data/genomes https://www.at-sphere.com/download/assemblies/LjRoot44.fna.gz
wget -P data/genomes https://www.at-sphere.com/download/assemblies/Root68.fna.gz
wget -P data/genomes https://www.at-sphere.com/download/assemblies/LjRoot303.fna.gz

gzip -d data/genomes/*Root*.fna.gz
ls -la data/genomes
head data/genomes/Root401.fna

## Do some parsing for At-sphere genomes to have a clear `-` separator
for genome in data/genomes/*Root*.fna; do
  sed -i 's/_/-/' $genome
done

head data/genomes/Root401.fna

# Amplicon
## Download
wget  https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/014/058/685/GCF_014058685.1_ASM1405868v1/GCF_014058685.1_ASM1405868v1_rna_from_genomic.fna.gz
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/009/425/GCF_000009425.1_ASM942v1/GCF_000009425.1_ASM942v1_rna_from_genomic.fna.gz
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/253/315/GCF_000253315.1_ASM25331v1/GCF_000253315.1_ASM25331v1_rna_from_genomic.fna.gz
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/714/595/GCF_000714595.1_ASM71459v1/GCF_000714595.1_ASM71459v1_rna_from_genomic.fna.gz
# Added 2026: B. subtilis NCIB 3610
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/002/055/965/GCF_002055965.1_ASM205596v1/GCF_002055965.1_ASM205596v1_rna_from_genomic.fna.gz

## Extract only 16S sequence from these 5 files and deal with multi-line fasta
gzip -d *.gz

ll *fna | wc -l
head GCF_000009425.1_ASM942v1_rna_from_genomic.fna
grep "16S ribosomal" *fna

for file in *_rna_from_genomic.fna; do
  genome=$(echo $file | cut -f1 -d ".")
  echo "Extracting 16S from $genome..."

  awk -v g="$genome" '
    # Find headers
    /^>/ {
      # Default: stop capturing once we hit a new header
      capture=0
      # Find headers from 16S sequences
      if ($0 ~ /16S ribosomal/) {
        # Turn on capturing for the following lines
        capture=1
        # Extract the identifier immediately after "rrna_"
        if (match($0, /rrna_([^ ]+)/, a)) {
          id=a[1]
          print ">" g "-" id
        } else {
          print ">" g "-unknown"
        }
      }
      next
    }
    # for all non-header lines print if capturing is on
    capture { print }
  ' "$file" > data/16S/${genome}_16S.fasta
done

## Added 2026: download AT-sphere 16S (root strains) into data/16S
wget -P data/16S https://www.at-sphere.com/download/rRNA_sequences/LjRoot60.fasta.gz
wget -P data/16S https://www.at-sphere.com/download/rRNA_sequences/LjRoot59.fasta.gz
wget -P data/16S https://www.at-sphere.com/download/rRNA_sequences/Root401.fasta.gz
wget -P data/16S https://www.at-sphere.com/download/rRNA_sequences/Root935.fasta.gz
wget -P data/16S https://www.at-sphere.com/download/rRNA_sequences/LjRoot44.fasta.gz
wget -P data/16S https://www.at-sphere.com/download/rRNA_sequences/Root68.fasta.gz
wget -P data/16S https://www.at-sphere.com/download/rRNA_sequences/LjRoot303.fasta.gz
gzip -d data/16S/*Root*.fasta.gz
ls -la data/16S

grep -c ">" data/16S/*.fasta
rm *fna
```

## Investigate 16S amplicon sequence

### Extract amplicon

Next, I used the primer information from the lab staff to extract the exact
amplicon sequence from the genome. I did this to check if we get more than one
amplicon and also compared the extracted sequence with the downloaded 16s.

rev_rc: AAGTCGTAACAAGGTAACCG

```{bash}
mkdir data/amplicons

# Run in silico PCR on all genomes
for genome in data/genomes/*fna; do
    id=$(basename $genome .fna)

    echo "-------------------------------------"
    echo "Start analysis of $id"
    echo "-------------------------------------"

    python scripts/insilico_pcr.py \
        --fasta $genome \
        --fasta_out ./${id}_16S_amplicon.fna \
        --fwd_primer AGAGTTTGATCMTGGCTCAG \
        --rev_primer CGGTTACCTTGTTACGACTT \
        --max_errors 1 \
        --min_len 1000 \
        --max_len 1600

done

# Run in silico PCR on published fasta for Root68
# (since fwd sits on end of contig when run on the genome and thus only a very short 16s is extracted)
python scripts/insilico_pcr.py \
        --fasta data/16S/Root68.fasta \
        --fasta_out data/amplicons/Root68_16S_amplicon.fna \
        --fwd_primer AGAGTTTGATCMTGGCTCAG \
        --rev_primer CGGTTACCTTGTTACGACTT \
        --max_errors 1 \
        --min_len 1000 \
        --max_len 1600


# To add: Move files to the right folder 
mv *amplicon.fna data/amplicons 
ls -la data/amplicons

# Standardize the name
sed -i "s/_/-/" data/amplicons/Root68_16S_amplicon.fna
ls -la data/amplicons
ll data/amplicons/*fna | wc -l

# Combine 42 amplicons (coming from 12 genomes)
grep -c ">" data/amplicons/*fna
grep -c ">" data/amplicons/*fna | awk -F':' '{sum += $2} END {print sum}'

cat data/amplicons/*.fna > data/amplicons/all_amplicons.fasta
```

#### Results of the in-silico PCR (2026 run)

Run on Crunchomics on 2026-11-06. For all genomes used in 2025, the
amplicons are identical to 2025 (same count, positions and lengths).

| Strain        | Genus             | 16S in annotation | Amplicons | Length (bp)  | Note |
|---------------|-------------------|------------------:|----------:|--------------|------|
| GCF_000009425 | Lactococcus       | 6                 | 6         | 1509         | |
| GCF_000253315 | Streptococcus     | 6                 | 6         | 1510         | |
| GCF_000714595 | Escherichia       | 9                 | 6         | 1470 to 1504 | 3 annotated 16S copies give no amplicon (see below) |
| GCF_002055965 | Bacillus          | 10                | 10        | 1511 to 1512 | New in 2026. Each amplicon lies inside one annotated 16S gene |
| GCF_014058685 | Lactobacillus     | 7                 | 7         | 1535         | |
| LjRoot303     | Streptomyces      | 1                 | 1         | 1448         | |
| LjRoot44      | Microbacterium    | 1                 | 1         | 1487         | |
| LjRoot59      | Pseudomonas       | 1                 | 1         | 1499         | |
| LjRoot60      | Pseudoxanthomonas | 1                 | 1         | 1507         | |
| Root401       | Pseudomonas       | 1                 | 1         | 1499         | |
| Root68        | Pseudomonas       | 1                 | 0         | (1386)       | No amplicon from the genome (see below). Taken from the AT-sphere 16S instead |
| Root935       | Flavobacterium    | 1                 | 1         | 1476         | |

- "16S in annotation": number of sequences in `data/16S` (NCBI annotation or
  AT-sphere 16S file).
- Total: 40 amplicons from 11 genomes, plus 1 for Root68 from the AT-sphere 16S.

Notes:

- **Root68**: the script finds only the forward primer
  (`Root68-contig_4`, position 457687) and no reverse primer. It stops with
  `ValueError: No plausible amplicon pairs found`. The loop continues with the
  next genome. The 2025 notes say the primer sits about 450 bp from the end of
  the contig. So the step after the loop runs the in-silico PCR on the
  AT-sphere 16S of Root68 instead. 2025 result:
  `Contig=Root68 start=1 end=1386 length=1386 orientation=fwd_to_end`.
- **GCF_000714595** (E. coli): 9 annotated 16S copies, 6 amplicons. 2025
  notes list 2 annotated copies without an amplicon:
  - `ECOLIN_RS22205_97`, location 4339815..4341330 (1515 bp)
  - `ECOLIN_RS27490_147`, location complement(5360896..5362258) (1362 bp)
- With `--max_len 2000`, GCF_000714595 gives even more matches (2025 note).
- Orientation: `fwd+rev_rc` means the gene is on the plus strand,
  `fwd_rc+rev` means it is on the minus strand.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

### Prepare amplicons for analysis

Next, I removed 100% identical sequences to better deal with multiple rrn
operons in the same genome. Genomes that still have more than one sequence are
clustered with vsearch at 99% identity. The centroids are named
`<genome>_1`, `<genome>_2`, ... The suffix also shows that a genome had more
than one 16S copy.

- 2025: 5 amplicons left for GCF_000714595, clustered into 2. 11 taxa, 12
  amplicon sequences.
- 2026: 22 sequences after deduplication. GCF_000714595 (Escherichia): 5 seqs
  into 2 clusters (as in 2025). GCF_002055965 (Bacillus): 7 seqs into 1
  cluster. 12 taxa, 13 amplicon sequences.

```{bash}
mkdir -p results/vsearch/

# Deduplicate at 100% identity
## 20 duplicated records removed
# 22 seqs kept
seqkit rmdup -s data/amplicons/all_amplicons.fasta \
  > data/amplicons/amplicons_nr.fasta

grep -c ">" data/amplicons/amplicons_nr.fasta

# Count sequences per genome after deduplication
grep ">" data/amplicons/amplicons_nr.fasta | sed 's/>//; s/-.*//' | sort | uniq -c

# Genomes with more than one sequence get clustered at 99% identity
# 2026: GCF_000714595 (Escherichia; 5 seqs) and GCF_002055965 (Bacillus; 7 seqs)
grep ">" data/amplicons/amplicons_nr.fasta | sed 's/>//; s/-.*//' | sort | uniq -c \
  | awk '$1 > 1 {print $2}' > data/amplicons/genomes_to_cluster.txt

cat data/amplicons/genomes_to_cluster.txt

conda activate vsearch_2.30.1

for genome in $(cat data/amplicons/genomes_to_cluster.txt); do
  echo "Clustering amplicons of $genome..."

  # Extract the sequences of this genome
  seqkit grep -r -p ${genome} data/amplicons/amplicons_nr.fasta \
    > results/vsearch/${genome}_amplicons.fasta
  
  grep -c ">" results/vsearch/${genome}_amplicons.fasta

  # Test if we can merge them
  vsearch --cluster_fast results/vsearch/${genome}_amplicons.fasta \
    --id 0.99 \
    --centroids results/vsearch/${genome}_centroids.fasta \
    --uc results/vsearch/${genome}_clusters.uc \
    --strand both \
    --query_cov 0.9

  # Clean IDs: <genome>_1, <genome>_2, ...
  awk -v g="$genome" '/^>/{i++ ; print ">" g "_" i ; next} {print}' \
    results/vsearch/${genome}_centroids.fasta \
    > results/vsearch/${genome}_centroids_clean.fasta
  
  grep -c ">" results/vsearch/${genome}_centroids_clean.fasta
done

# 2026 results:
# GCF_000714595: 5 seqs (1470 to 1504 bp) -> 2 clusters (sizes 4 and 1)
# GCF_002055965: 7 seqs (1511 to 1512 bp) -> 1 cluster (size 7)

# Combine: remove all copies of the clustered genomes, append their centroids, trim headers
# Note: amplicons_nr_final will be named amplicons_nr.fasta for the tutorial
# results/vsearch must hold only centroid files from this run
seqkit grep -v -r -f data/amplicons/genomes_to_cluster.txt data/amplicons/amplicons_nr.fasta | \
  cat - results/vsearch/*_centroids_clean.fasta | \
  awk '/^>/{sub(/-.*/,"")}1' > data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final.fasta

# 2026: 13 seqs
# GCF_000009425, GCF_000253315, GCF_014058685, LjRoot303, LjRoot44, LjRoot59,
# LjRoot60, Root401, Root68, Root935, GCF_000714595_1, GCF_000714595_2, GCF_002055965_1
grep -c ">" data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final.fasta
grep ">" data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final.fasta

# Compare sequence identity
# Matching query sequences: 12 of 13 (92.31%)
vsearch --allpairs_global data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final.fasta \
        --acceptall --maxaccepts 0 \
        --blast6out results/vsearch/amplicons_identity.tsv

conda deactivate

# Create summary
python scripts/pivot_vsearch.py
less -S results/vsearch/amplicons_identity_matrix.csv

# Make one db with all E.coli sequences
awk '/^>/ {
  header=$0
  # Extract genome name (before the first '-')
  if (match(header, /^>([^-]+)-/, a)) genome=a[1]
  else if (match(header, /^>([^_]+)_/, a)) genome=a[1]
  else genome=substr(header, 2)
  count[genome]++
  print ">" genome "-" count[genome]
  next
} !/^>/ { print }' data/amplicons/amplicons_nr.fasta > data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_clean.fasta

```

## Make the files for teaching_material/data (added 2026)

In 2025 these steps were not recorded. `accession_to_genus.tsv` was probably
made by hand. All three products go into one folder,
`data/for_teaching_material`, to copy them to the repo in one go.

- `<id>.fasta.gz`: the 16S sequences of one strain, for the student
  exercises in `cli.qmd`. These are the files in `data/16S`, gzipped. The
  2025 files in the repo have the same headers, sequence counts and line
  layout as `data/16S`.
- `amplicons_nr.fasta`: a copy of `data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final.fasta`.
- `accession_to_genus.tsv`: one line per header in `amplicons_nr.fasta`, with
  its genus. It is made from the fasta headers, so the IDs match the
  reference exactly. The genus per strain comes from a small lookup table,
  typed in from `teaching_material/data/strains_2026.tsv`.

```{bash}
mkdir -p data/for_teaching_material

# Student files: one gzipped 16S fasta per strain
# NCBI files are named <id>_16S.fasta, AT-sphere files <id>.fasta
for file in data/16S/*.fasta; do
  id=$(basename $file .fasta | sed 's/_16S$//')
  echo "Compressing $file into data/for_teaching_material/${id}.fasta.gz"
  gzip -c $file > data/for_teaching_material/${id}.fasta.gz
done

ls -la data/for_teaching_material

# 2026: same counts as the 2025 files in teaching_material/data
# GCF_000009425: 6, GCF_000253315: 6, GCF_000714595: 9, GCF_014058685: 7,
# 7 root strains: 1 each. New: GCF_002055965: 10
for file in data/for_teaching_material/*.fasta.gz; do
  echo "$file: $(zcat $file | grep -c '>') sequences"
done

# Reference for minimap2 (named amplicons_nr.fasta in the tutorial)
cp data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final.fasta data/for_teaching_material/amplicons_nr.fasta
grep -c ">" data/for_teaching_material/amplicons_nr.fasta

# Lookup table: strain ID -> genus, typed in from strains_2026.tsv
printf "GCF_000009425\tLactococcus\n"        >  data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "GCF_000253315\tStreptococcus\n"      >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "GCF_000714595\tEscherichia\n"        >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "GCF_002055965\tBacillus\n"           >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "GCF_014058685\tLactobacillus\n"      >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "LjRoot60\tPseudoxanthomonas\n"       >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "LjRoot59\tPseudomonas\n"             >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "Root401\tPseudomonas\n"              >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "Root935\tFlavobacterium\n"           >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "LjRoot44\tMicrobacterium\n"          >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "Root68\tPseudomonas\n"               >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv
printf "LjRoot303\tStreptomyces\n"           >> data/strain_to_genus.tsv

cat data/strain_to_genus.tsv

# All headers of the final reference, one per line, without ">"
grep ">" data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final.fasta | sed 's/>//' \
  > data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final_ids.txt

cat data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final_ids.txt

# Give each header its genus
# Headers with a copy number at the end (e.g. GCF_000714595_1) are not in the
# lookup table, so remove the copy number (_1, _2) and look up the strain ID
awk -F'\t' '
  # First file: the lookup table
  NR==FNR { genus[$1]=$2; next }
  # Second file: one header per line
  {
    strain=$1
    if (!(strain in genus)) sub(/_[0-9]+$/, "", strain)
    print $1 "\t" genus[strain]
  }' data/strain_to_genus.tsv data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final_ids.txt \
  > data/for_teaching_material/accession_to_genus.tsv

# 2026: 13 lines, one per header in amplicons_nr_final.fasta, no header without genus.
# Same as the 2025 file plus GCF_002055965_1 Bacillus, minus the unused line GCF_000714595
cat data/for_teaching_material/accession_to_genus.tsv
wc -l data/amplicons/amplicons_nr_final_ids.txt data/for_teaching_material/accession_to_genus.tsv

# Headers without a genus (this should print nothing)
awk -F'\t' '$2==""' data/for_teaching_material/accession_to_genus.tsv
```

Copy `data/for_teaching_material/*` into `teaching_material/data/`.

Differences to the 2025 `accession_to_genus.tsv`:

- 2025 also had a line `GCF_000714595  Escherichia` without a copy number.
  No header in `amplicons_nr.fasta` has this ID, so the line was not used.
  The new file leaves it out.
- 2025 had no newline after the last line.
